accepted.question_text: Determine the exact enumeration and asymptotic growth of permutations that avoid the classical pattern 1324. In particular, determine the Stanley-Wilf limit for 1324-avoiding permutations and, if possible, an exact formula or asymptotic description for the number of 1324-avoiders of length n.

evidence.quote: Here I will essentially only treat one unresolved case, that of the only classical pattern of length 4, up to Wilf equivalence, for which neither exact enumeration nor asymptotics have been determined.
The only Wilf class of patterns of length 4 for which the Stanley-Wilf limit is unknown is represented by 1324.

accepted.question_text: Prove or refute the conjectured upper bound SW(1324) < e*pi*sqrt(2/3) for the Stanley-Wilf limit of the classical pattern 1324.

evidence.quote: In [23] it is conjectured that SW(1324) < eπ√2/3 ≈ 13.001954.

accepted.question_text: Prove or refute that for every fixed inversion count k, the number of 1324-avoiding permutations of length n having exactly k inversions is an increasing function of n.

evidence.quote: This would follow from another conjecture in [23], which says that the number of 1324-avoiders of length n with a fixed number k of inversions is increasing as a function of n.

accepted.question_text: For each pattern length k, determine whether the largest Stanley-Wilf limit among all classical patterns of length k is always attained by a layered pattern.

evidence.quote: One of the weakest of these conjectures, widely believed to be true, is made explicit in [23, Conjecture 1] (although it may have been made before) and says that among all patterns of a given length k, the largest Stanley-Wilf limit is attained by some layered pattern.

accepted.question_text: For each positive integer k, determine the form of the layered permutation pattern of length k that is avoided by the largest number of permutations, equivalently the layered pattern of length k that is most easily avoided.

evidence.quote: It is still unclear, however, what form the most avoided layered pattern of length k has, although there are conjectures for particular families of values of k that seem reasonable, while others (in an abundance of conjectures, published and unpublished) have been shown false.

accepted.question_text: For every even integer k, prove or refute that the layered pattern of length k with layers (1, 2, 2, ..., 2, 2, 1) is the most avoided pattern among all patterns of length k.

evidence.quote: For example, a conjecture of Kézdy and Snevily [18, Conj. 9.10] that has not been refuted is that for patterns of even length k the most avoided pattern is the one with layers (1, 2, 2, . . . , 2, 2, 1).

accepted.question_text: For every integer k congruent to 1 modulo 4, prove or refute that the most avoided pattern of length k is the layered pattern with symmetric layer sizes (1, 2, ..., 2, 3, 2, ..., 2, 1).

evidence.quote: Also, Burstein’s Conjecture 9.11 in [18] that for k ≡ 1 (mod 4) the most avoided pattern of length k has symmetric layers (1, 2, . . . , 2, 3, 2, . . . , 2, 1) still stands.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exist two permutation patterns whose avoidance counts switch relative order more than once, and in particular whether two patterns can switch places infinitely often as n grows.

evidence.quote: It is still unknown whether such a switch occurs twice or more for any pair of patterns, but Stankova and West conjecture [42, Conjecture 2] that this does not happen.
They also make the weaker conjecture that for any pair of patterns σ and τ there is an N such that either Avσ(n) < Avτ(n) for all n > N or else the opposite inequality holds for all n > N.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the bound 2.25*k^2 is the best possible general upper bound for the Stanley-Wilf limit of a classical permutation pattern of length k.

evidence.quote: If the conjecture is true that the most avoided pattern of length k, for any given k, is a layered pattern then this would be an upper bound for the Stanley-Wilf limit of any pattern of length k, but it is not known whether this bound is the best possible.

accepted.question_text: Characterize completely the intervals [σ, τ] in the permutation pattern poset whose Möbius function satisfies μ(σ, τ) = 0.

evidence.quote: Although many families of intervals [σ, τ] with µ(σ, τ) = 0 are described in [19, 46], it is an open problem to characterise such intervals completely.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the intervals [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset for which the absolute value |μ(σ, π)| of the Möbius function equals the number of occurrences of σ in π.

evidence.quote: It might also be interesting to characterise those intervals for which |µ(σ, π)| equals the number of occurrences of σ in π.

accepted.question_text: Find a bound for |μ(σ, τ)| in the permutation pattern poset that depends only on the number of occurrences of σ in τ, without requiring additional structure such as separability.

evidence.quote: Another question raised in [19] is whether it is possible to find a bound on |µ(σ, τ)| that depends only on the number of occurrences of σ in τ.

accepted.question_text: Determine for which permutations σ and π the order complex Δ(σ, π) of the interior of the interval [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset has the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres.

evidence.quote: 1. For which σ and π does ∆(σ, π) have the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres?

accepted.question_text: Let Γ be the subcomplex of Δ(σ, π) induced by those permutations τ in the interval [σ, π] with μ(σ, τ) not equal to 0. Determine whether Γ must always be pure, meaning that all of its maximal simplices have the same dimension.

evidence.quote: 2. Let Γ be the subcomplex of ∆(σ, π) induced by those elements τ of [σ, π] for which µ(σ, τ) 6= 0. Is Γ a pure complex, that is, do all its maximal simplices (with respect to inclusion) have the same dimension?

accepted.question_text: If a permutation σ occurs precisely once in a permutation π and the Möbius function of the interval [σ, π] is μ(σ, π) = ±1, determine whether the order complex Δ(σ, π) must be homotopy equivalent to a sphere.

evidence.quote: 3. If σ occurs precisely once in π, and µ(σ, π) = ±1, is ∆(σ, π) homotopy equivalent to a sphere?

accepted.question_text: Determine for which permutations σ and π the order complex Δ(σ, π) associated with the interval [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset is shellable.

evidence.quote: 4. For which σ and π is ∆(σ, π) shellable?

accepted.question_text: Prove a general finite-check theorem for linear combinations of vincular patterns: if two such combinations have the same distribution on permutations of all lengths up to some bound depending only on the pattern lengths involved, then they have the same distribution for all lengths.

evidence.quote: A general theorem to this effect, guaranteeing that checking such equidistributions for small n is sufficient to establish equidistribution for all n, would be a major breakthrough, provided the values that need to be checked are small enough, since that would give automatic proofs of various theorems.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the ring of functions generated by vincular patterns has algebraic relations beyond the known upgrading relation, and if so describe those additional relations.

evidence.quote: Since this ring contains all linear combinations of vincular patterns, it might be worthwhile to study its algebraic structure further. In particular, it would be interesting to know if there are other relations in this ring.

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary permutation class C, determine whether the growth-rate definition gr(C) = lim sup_{n->infinity} |C_n|^(1/n) can always be strengthened by replacing the lim sup with an actual limit.

evidence.quote: One of the most natural open questions is whether the limit superior above in the definition can be replaced by a limit; this is known to be possible in the case of singleton-based classes by Arratia [5].

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the conjectures of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris become true when restricted to finitely based permutation classes, despite being false in full generality.

evidence.quote: It remains open if, as suggested by Klazar [33], the conjectures of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris hold when restricted to finitely based permutation classes.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the possible growth rates of permutation classes in the interval between κ ≈ 2.21 and λ ≈ 2.48, where κ is the least accumulation point of accumulation points of growth rates and λ is the threshold above which every real number occurs as a growth rate of some permutation class.

evidence.quote: Thus a striking problem remains: To characterise the growth rates between κ and λ.
